headline: QA and testing covers five items — an automated test suite, a QA report with test cases and bugs, security hardening tests, workflow-feature tests, and UI/UX testing — and the code review was unable to confirm or rule out any of them.
what_is_there: The tickets describe automated tests across the product (workflow engine, routing, transfers, security features) plus manual QA activity such as executed test cases, documented bugs, and UI/UX testing. What the review actually saw was production code — configuration, connectors, history, and the workflow user interface — with no test files or QA artefacts among it.
what_is_unclear: Whether any of these tests or QA records exist is unconfirmed: the files examined were a keyword-selected subset that happened to contain no tests, and a supporting document referenced by the tickets was explicitly about a different codebase. This is an absence of evidence, not evidence that the testing work is missing.
suggested_action: Ask the team to point directly at where the tests and QA outputs live — the test folder, the test run results, and the bug list — so the area can be checked against the real artefacts rather than inferred from application code.
caveat: One referenced supporting document does not describe this repository, so any ticket detail drawn from it should be re-checked with the team.
